lede: Tom built a big man's team, and it finished on the podium: fifth seed, 12–7, third place. It won field-goal percentage in 20 of 22 matchups, and that was the foundation. The odd part is the money. $42 of the $200 went on Trae Young, and he never played a minute in a Brighton lineup — he was on the Foxes before opening night, in the deal that brought back Josh Hart, who lasted ten days. 60% of what this team scored came from players it did not draft, and Nikola Jokic arrived on day 72.
profile:
Read the table top to bottom and the build is obvious. First in the league in FG% at .503, second in rebounds, third in blocks. Last in threes — 879 against a league average of 1,173 — and 13th in turnovers. A roster of centres pays for it in threes and giveaways, and that is a coherent trade: five categories won at 64% or better.

The threes were a punt (4–17–1). Free throws and steals at 36% were not. Those are the two categories where the shape leaked more than it had to.
ledger: 104 of 198 categories, playoffs included. Six regular-season weeks came down to a single category, and Brighton won five of them — the margin that turns a 4.5-a-week team into a 12–7 record. The soft patch was weeks 15 to 17: 2–6–1, 3–5–1, 3–5–1. The playoffs went the other way. A 7–2 win over The Infirmary, a 4–4–1 draw with Fantastic 5 that sent Fantastic 5 through, and a 7–2 win over Optimize the MVPs for third.
draft: The two picks that stayed did the work. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at $79 banked 2,772, the most on the roster, and Evan Mobley at $37 added 1,912. Matas Buzelis at $8 was the value pick: 1,759 banked, 220 per dollar, on the roster until day 150. Kyshawn George at $1 returned 537 per dollar before being traded. The rest of the board moved fast. Trae Young ($42) and Kon Knueppel ($1) were gone before the first lineup. Knueppel turned up on Fast and Curryous within a week and finished with 2,392 for the season, third-most of all thirteen Brighton picks. Neemias Queta and Dennis Schroder were packaged on day 5, and Deni Avdija and Onyeka Okongwu on day 72.
production: Sixty percent from outside the draft, and the best of it was found early. Amen Thompson (2,230) and Ryan Rollins (1,993) were the second- and third-highest scorers on the team, both on the roster from the first week without being drafted here. Jokic is the headline. 1,394 banked in 28 games is 50 a game — close to double the rate of anyone else in the lineup.
trades: Seven trades recovered of the nine ESPN counts. The four that can be graded on both sides all come out negative on total production: −831, −484, −584 and −36. That grade needs one caveat. It counts totals, so any two-for-one looks bad by construction. Day 72 — Avdija and Okongwu for Jokic — is the clearest case. Two players who went on to produce 2,220 elsewhere, for one who produced 1,636 in 33 games. With ten starting slots a day and a wire to fill the spare roster spot, taking the best player in the sport at 50 a game is a defensible trade even if the column says −584. Day 5 is harder to defend: Queta and Schroder for Okongwu, and Queta went on to 1,586. So is day 49: Kyshawn George for Franz Wagner, who played ten more games all season.
wire: 56 claims won from 210 attempts, $98 of FAAB, top bid $21. The average swap returned 0.42 net production a day over the following fortnight — 9th of 14, hit rate 40%. The best claim came early: Jaime Jaquez Jr. on day 13, +13.6 a day, and Jaquez went on to bank 1,388. The wire was not where this team got better: its best additions arrived by trade or in the first week.
bench: Fifteen wasted player-days, sixth in the league, and one bad day accounts for a lot of it. Day 104: OG Anunoby 42, Ryan Rollins 39, Jalen Duren 36 and Ivica Zubac 35, all on the bench at once — 152 production sitting down in week 15, a matchup lost 2–6–1. Whether there was room to start them depends on who held the slots that day. Either way, it was the worst day of the season.
last: The third-place game, and Brighton treated it like a final. 70 starting slots set against 68, 44 of them producing a game against 39, and a 7–2 win. Rebounds 271 to 199, blocks 30 to 11 — the season's shape, intact in its last week.
closing:
A good season, honestly earned. The identity was clear from the draft — bigs, field-goal percentage, the glass — and it held for twenty-two weeks and a podium finish.

Two things to take into next year. First, premium money went on players the team never kept: $42 on a guard gone before opening night, and a $1 rookie given away who outscored everyone but the $79 star. Second, the trades bought quality at the cost of volume, and two of them (day 5 and day 49) gave away more than they brought.

And decide on the leaks. Threes were a real punt. Free throws and steals at 36% were not, and a single guard held all year would have turned some of those into wins.
